strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with elementwise scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with element-wise scale/unscale operations between each stage, exactly as the reference implementation. Requires 8 all-reduce dispatches plus local scaling operations. Represents the baseline with maximum dispatch count but simplest logic.

strategies.name: Fused scaling into tensor views
strategies.desc: Precomputes all scaling coefficient products across the 8 stages and materializes them as a single scaling vector, then performs all 8 all-reduces on pre-scaled shards with a final single unscale operation. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches but fuses all elementwise operations into 2 total scaling passes (one pre-scale, one post-scale), reducing memory traffic.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter followed by all-gather chain
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into a reduce-scatter (each rank gets 1/W of the result) followed by all-gather to reconstruct the full vector. For 8 stages this yields 16 collective dispatches but each collective operates on smaller payloads, potentially better pipelining on high world-size with Trainium's interconnect topology.

strategies.name: Batched multi-stage all-reduce
strategies.desc: Groups multiple stages together by pre-allocating a larger buffer containing multiple copies of the vector, applies scaling transformations on all copies, then dispatches a single large all-reduce covering multiple stages at once. Reduces dispatch count from 8 to 2-4 dispatches by trading increased payload size (2-4x larger) for fewer kernel launches.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction
strategies.desc:
Exploits potential node boundaries by first performing intra-node reductions (if num_nodes > 1) using node-local all-reduce, then inter-node reduction, then broadcasting back. Each of 8 stages uses 3 collectives (intra-reduce, inter-reduce, broadcast) for 24 total dispatches, but each operates on smaller payloads proportional to nodes/devices-per-node, optimizing for NUMA/interconnect hierarchy.
